user.t:
READ-ONLY deep research. Fetch and read PRIMARY pages, not just snippets. Do not create or edit files; return text only. Cite the URL and date for every claim, and grade A/B/C.

Context: scoup.ai is pre-product. It does AI evidence packets, demand letters, deadline tracking and dispute filing for detention and accessorial recovery, for mid-market shippers and small carriers, paid on contingency. The founder is in Norway. A first research pass found these as the key threats and channels; go deep on them:
1. Loop (loop.com, $95M Series C, Apr 2026). What exactly does its Exception Agent do? Does it cover road detention and accessorials, and for shippers or carriers? Who are its customers, and what is its pricing model? What is its roadmap language?
2. co3.io. Who are they? They write about road-freight detention recovery and geofencing for forwarders (Jun/Aug 2026). Product, customers, region (EU?), and funding.
3. Nuvocargo's "$47K detention recovery gap: why mid-market shippers leave money on the table". Read it. What do they offer, and what is the methodology behind the $47K?
4. Opereit (Barcelona, $2.5M pre-seed Jun 2026). Exactly which claims do they automate?
5. Telematics developer and marketplace programs as a data channel: Motive Marketplace, Geotab Marketplace, Samsara App Marketplace, Platform Science.
   - Can a third-party app get a carrier's geofence and dwell data with consent?
   - Partner requirements, fees and revenue share.
   - Which detention apps are already listed (DockClock, FleetOptos, GeoStamp)?
   - What would it take for scoup.ai to be listed?
6. Factoring companies (Triumph/TriumphPay, OTR Solutions, RTS, Apex, Bobtail): do they collect detention or accessorials for carriers today? On what terms? Are they a channel (white-label recovery) or a competitor?
7. FMCSA broker-transparency rule: current status as of Oct 2026 (final rule? second NPRM?). Effective dates and the exact carrier rights.
Output ≤ 1000 words, organised by item, ending with a "so what for scoup.ai" line for each.

handback.t:
Research report, run 2026-10-10. Grades: A = primary page fetched, B = primary page fetched but thin or only part of the claim, C = secondary or snippet only. No files were written, per your read-only instruction. That means I did not write the run-contract marker and did not store anything. I also did NOT run aidefence_scan on the fetched text, so treat the record as screened=false. Nothing below is quoted verbatim beyond short phrases. Spend is unmeasured.

**1. Loop (Exception Agent)**
- The Exception Agent is an autonomous agent that detects carrier-invoice discrepancies, opens disputes by email with the carrier, reads replies, pulls supporting documents and tracks the dispute to correct payment. It follows customer-set policies, flags hard cases for human review, and keeps an audit trail. [loop.com/technology/exception-agent](https://loop.com/technology/exception-agent) (fetched 2026-10-10) A. [Deep-dive post, 15 May 2026](https://www.loop.com/article/a-deep-dive-with-loops-exception-agent-automatically-manage-freight-disputes) B.
- Funding: $95M Series C in April 2026, about $160M total, led by Valor. It is positioned as expanding "beyond freight audit into full logistics". [Loop announcement](https://www.loop.com/article/loop-raises-95m-series-c-to-scale-its-ai-platform-across-the-supply-chain) B. The funding details come from search snippets (C); the page fetch returned almost nothing on the agent.
- Detention and accessorials: a search snippet attributed to the deep-dive page says agents check whether residential and appointment fees and detention charges are "calculated correctly". When I fetched the page, it did not mention detention or accessorials. So Loop checks charges that carriers billed. It does not generate claims from telematics. C.
- Customers are shippers, i.e. AP and transportation teams. Named logos: Michael Kors, Under Armour, General Mills, Macy's, J. Crew, Great Dane. It covers parcel, LTL, FTL, ocean and air at platform level, and the page does not say which of those the agent covers. A/B. It has no carrier-side offering.
- Pricing: nothing for the agent. Loop publicly argues against gain-share and for SaaS subscription. [Loop post](https://loop.com/article/gain-share-pricing-is-broken) C (snippet). Customers cite 2-7% savings.
- Roadmap language: one line, "for teams that pay first and recover later, a credit-chasing workflow is planned for the future". B.
- So what for scoup.ai: Loop is an enterprise-shipper audit tool, seen on its subscription model and enterprise logos. Contingency pricing for the mid-market and carriers is the gap. The "credit-chasing" line is a drift signal to watch, but it is not detention recovery.

**2. CO3 (co3.io)**
- It is a European telematics aggregator with offices in Wrocław and Berlin. It claims "500+ integrations across trucks, trailers, and subcontractors". It offers visibility, ETA, geofence dwell timestamps, and CO2 reporting. The detention post is [Aug 11, 2026](https://co3.io/news/geofencing-detention-recovery-freight-forwarders) (fetched) A/B.
- The buyers are forwarders, hauliers and mixed fleets. Named customers: sennder, Futura Cargo, Seifert Transport. The detention pitch is "a geofence stamps arrival and departure so a forwarder can bill the shipper". It cites 25-40% improvement from "North American 
[...]
 is an EU data and evidence provider for forwarders. It is not a claims filer and does not work on contingency. It is a possible data partner, or a competitor if it adds filing. It is the relevant benchmark if you sell in Europe or Norway.

**3. Nuvocargo $47K article (Apr 23, 2026, Sebastián Salgado)**
- [Article](https://nuvocargo.com/blog-posts/the-47k-detention-recovery-gap-why-mid-market-shippers-leave-money-on-the-table). The $47K average annual uncollected detention and the "60% improvement in collection rates" cite only "Nuvocargo Platform Analytics" and "our platform data". The fetched text gave no sample size, period, definition of mid-market, or formula. A for that finding: there is no disclosed methodology.
- Nuvocargo is a US<>Mexico brokerage, managed transportation, customs and AI-TMS company. The article is content marketing for its TMS, not a recovery service.
- So what for scoup.ai: do not cite $47K as market evidence. Nuvocargo does not run contingency recovery, so it is not a direct rival. Run your own measurement on synthetic or pilot data; this also fits the CLAUDE.md honesty rule.

**4. Opereit (Barcelona, $2.5M pre-seed, Jun 12, 2026)**
- [AI Insider](https://theaiinsider.tech/?p=48489) B. Co-led by Seedcamp and Yellow. Founded 2025 by Pablo Cousin. It automates carrier-invoice reconciliation/audit and claims for lost or damaged shipments. The article does not mention delays or returns. Customers: Amphora Logistics, Nude Project, Ecoalf, which are e-commerce brands and retail logistics, so likely parcel and fulfilment (my inference).
- No evidence it covers road detention or accessorial dispute filing.
- So what for scoup.ai: Opereit is an adjacent EU competitor in damage and loss claims for e-commerce. It is not in detention. If it expands, it would be the first European startup to compete for the same shipper-side spend.

**5. Telematics marketplaces**
- Motive: GeoStamp (WiseTech) is listed. It uses push "Vehicle Locations" to detect geofence entry and exit, and it targets drayage and terminals. [Listing](https://marketplace.gomotive.com/app/geostamp-by-wisetech-global.md) A. Motive's page describes a developer/tech partner program with "co-marketing incentives and revenue sharing", but no percentages, fees or consent mechanics were found. [Motive partner terms](https://gomotive.com/legal/partner-program-terms-of-service/): those are an affiliate PartnerStack referral model (commission paid within 45 days after month-end). They are not marketplace revenue share. B/C.
- Geotab: four partner tiers (Basic, Standard, Premier, Order Now). Basic means SDK-only, with no review. The upper tiers have legal, technical and security vetting. You build first, then apply to the Marketplace team. Data comes from MyGeotab API feeds. Fees and revenue share are only in a FAQ I did not reach. [Geotab](https://marketplace.geotab.com/integrate-geotab/) A/B. FleetOptos Detention Tracker is listed and uses Geotab dwell data. [FleetOptos](https://marketplace.geotab.com/solutions/fleetoptos/) C.
- Samsara: apply to the Technology Partner Program with a company email, "Build a technical integration", use case, status and customer interest. A weekly review gives an answer in 5-7 business days, then Partner Developer Portal access. OAuth 2.0 is recommended, so customers grant access by themselves. It asks about Europe plans. Listing steps, fees and revenue share are not in the docs. [Samsara](https://developers.samsara.com/docs/application-process) A/B. I did not verify the DockClock/Samsara listing.
- Platform Science: [DockClock](https://www.platformscience.com/marketplace/dockclock) is listed. It auto-tracks detention, notifies customers, follows up and pushes line items to the invoice. C/B.
- Consent-based customer data access is possible via OAuth, tokens or Geotab SDK. Revenue share and fee numbers are unverified everywhere. I found no public figures. The Geotab $5-25 per vehicle per month figure is an industry estimate (C).
- So what for scoup.ai: a carrier connects its own telematics account (OAuth on Samsara; Motive and Geotab are likely similar, unverified). Start with Samsara's weekly-review program, and build Geotab Basic as a no-cost start. Ask each program's team about fees and revenue share in writing. Note that DockClock, FleetOptos and GeoStamp already own "track detention". Your wedge is the demand letter and filing after tracking.

**6. Factoring companies**
- OTR Solutions: tools to document and collect detention. A mobile upload app, a portal to track claims, an operations team that "supports carriers through the collection process", and non-recourse factoring that pays "even when detention charges are disputed". The page says it does not collect on carriers' behalf. [OTR](https://otrsolutions.com/detention-pay-in-trucking/) A. No fees stated.
- TriumphPay: payment network with about $51.3B annual brokered freight. Apex joined it in May 2025. Net-2 QuickPay costs 2% (C). I found no detention-collection service from RTS, Apex, Bobtail or TriumphPay. This is an absence in a snippet search only, not verified.
- So what for scoup.ai: factors fund and verify invoices but do not pursue detention disputes. That makes them a plausible white-label channel, since their carriers' detention invoices are the ones that get disputed. OTR's "disputed charges" non-recourse line is the closest overlap. This is a hypothesis; test it with one conversation.

**7. FMCSA broker transparency (49 CFR Part 371, RIN 2126-AC63)**
- As of Sep 30, 2026 it is still a proposal, not a final rule. The first NPRM was published in Nov 2024. FMCSA sent a supplemental NPRM to OIRA on Aug 27, 2026, after missing May and July targets. OIRA has up to 90 days, i.e. to about late Nov 2026. After publication comes a new comment round, then a final rule, so no effective date exists. [FreightWaves](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/broker-transparency-proposal-clears-fmcsa-and-heads-to-the-white-house) A/B.
- Proposed carrier rights: brokers keep transaction records electronically and give copies to a carrier or shipper within 48 hours of a request. The records must show charges, freight description, amounts, dates and claims. Contract waivers of that right may be barred, which makes it a duty on the broker. OOIDA and others asked for automatic sharing. The text is confidential until it clears review, so the details could change.
- So what for scoup.ai: do not build a product feature or marketing claim on this rule yet. If it becomes final, it would help you get broker records as evidence, but it is probably 2027 at the earliest. It does not directly cover detention.
